subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Thornton <jamie@shoply.com>, Asha Menon <asha@shoply.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Jamie / Asha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps we discussed. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Heavy spend and rate limits on current OpenAI + Anthropic usage leading to throttling during peak hours.
- Loss of control over model versions and limited ability to run in VPC for sensitive flows.
- Rising token costs impacting margin on high-volume user journeys (search autocomplete / content gen).

Current stack (as described):
- Frontend: React + Next.js; backend services on AWS (ECS + RDS).
- Primary API usage: OpenAI gpt-4.1 for customer-facing generation; Anthropic Claude for safety/classification.
- Some in-house caching layer but limited prefix/KV caching for long conversations.

Success criteria for a migration:
1) Cost reduction of >= 30% on per-unit inference costs while maintaining output quality.
2) Drop-in compatibility with existing prompts and safety classifiers (minimal prompt engineering).
3) Ability to run a private deployment in our VPC for PII-sensitive flows.
4) Predictable latency < 400ms p50 for typical prompts; throughput target of ~120 qps peak.

Compatibility/constraints you called out:
- Need to keep function/tool-calling semantics and the existing prompt->response JSON parsing used today.
- Must support streaming for the product editor flows.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 plus audit logs and KMS integration for keys.

Model shortlist (preliminary):
- Llama 3 70B (quantized) for generation workloads
- Mistral-instruct variants for instruction-tuned tasks
- Claude-compatible open checkpoints for classification workloads (or a retrain of an open model)

Next steps (agreed):
1) Redwood to share a short compatibility checklist + model-runbook for Shoply to review (Rishi).
2) Shoply to send current monthly token ranges and a representative prompt set (~50 prompts) for quality benchmarking.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Shoply engs next week (30–45m).

Attachments: I attached a short MAP (Shoply-MAP-v0.3.pdf) with the proposed milestones and responsibilities, and our standard security questionnaire stub (security-questionnaire-2027.docx).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with available slots for the technical session.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Jamie Thornton <jamie@shoply.com>

Date: 2027-04-18T15:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Thanks Marissa — this is a great summary and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications / notes from our side:

- Current spend: roughly $95k/month between OpenAI and Anthropic; we spike to ~200k tokens/min during promos.
- We use OpenAI for generation and Anthropic for safety/classification (callout: Claude has better recall on our internal taxonomy today).
- Streaming is required for the editor; we currently rely on server-sent events.
- For private deployment, our security team will need a clear KMS integration plan and audit log retention details.

Action items from our side:
- I’ll share a sample prompt set by EOD Friday (we sanitize PII).
- Scheduling: next Wed or Thu morning PT works for engineering deep-dive.

One question for Rishi: are there known drop-in API patterns you use to emulate OpenAI/Anthropic tool-calling semantics? We’d prefer minimal app changes.

Cheers,
Jamie
Head of Integrations | Shoply
jamie@shoply.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Thornton <jamie@shoply.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Jamie — looping in answers to your API/compatibility question and giving a quick sense of the technical approach.

Short answers up-front:
- Yes — Redwood provides a compatibility layer and sample wrappers that mirror OpenAI/Anthropic call patterns (including streaming and function-calling semantics). That reduces app changes to adapter-level plumbing in most cases.
- For classification/safety, we recommend running a tuned smaller model with a lightweight ensemble pre-filter that mimics your Claude behavior (we have benchmark kits).

What we’ll propose for Shoply (high level):
1) Compatibility shim: an API proxy that translates current OpenAI/Anthropic call shapes to Redwood runtime endpoints. Can be deployed in your VPC or as a managed connector.
2) Model recommendations for your workloads (benchmarked against your 50 prompts):
   - Primary generation: Llama 3 70B quant (with Redwood-verified latencies)
   - Instruction-tuned fallback: Mistral-Instruct-7B v2 (for cheaper, high-throughput paths)
   - Safety/classification: Claude-like ensemble using a fine-tuned 7–13B model + simple rules layer
3) Ops: KV/prefix caching for conversational flows, batching for high-throughput paths, and autoscaling policies for promos.

Attachments in this thread include the MAP Marissa attached — I’ve also dropped a one-pager with our compatibility checklist in the Drive link Marissa shared.

Next up from my side: I’ll prepare the compatibility checklist and an initial benchmark plan. I can take the lead on the technical deep-dive — suggest we block 45 minutes; I’ll send a calendar invite for Thu 10:00 AM PT unless Wed is preferred.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
